state.misconception_label: Assumes that an arrow on a number line starts at zero

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: ![Number line with -12 and -7 marked. Starting at -12, follow an arrow pointing to the right labelled +10. Then there is an arrow labelled b pointing to the left, which ends at -7 on the number line.]() What is the value of \( b \) ? I got \( -7 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: It looks like you may be assuming that the arrow on the number line starts at zero. Let's revisit the concept of starting points on a number line and how they relate to the values being represented. Can you think about where the arrow actually starts in relation to the numbers -12 and -7? Let's work through this step by step.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so the arrow doesn't start at zero... it starts at -12, doesn't it? So I need to follow the +10 arrow first to see where that takes me, and then work out what b is from there?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Great job recognizing that the arrow doesn't start at zero, but at -12 instead. Now, focus on following the path of the +10 arrow to see where it leads you on the number line. Think about how the values change as you move along the number line from -12. This will help you determine the value of \( b \). Keep up the good work!

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: So if I start at -12 and go right by +10, that would be -12 + 10 which equals -2, right? Then the arrow b goes left from -2 to -7, so b would be... -5? Is that how you work out the value of the arrow?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher explicitly names and addresses the zero-starting-point misconception, uses appropriate questioning to guide reasoning, and the student successfully corrects their understanding, moving from -7 to the correct answer of -5 through proper number line reasoning.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher exemplifies the constructive strategy by breaking the problem into manageable steps (first identifying the starting point, then following the +10 arrow, then determining b), scaffolding within the student's ZPD by addressing the misconception about starting at zero, and adjusting support as the student progresses from confusion to correct reasoning.
